business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) Cryogenic Pumps

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid legal system: Civil law codification (Egyptian Civil Code No. 131/1948; Commercial Code No. 17/1999) with Islamic Sharia as the principal source of legislation under Article 2 of the 2014 Constitution. Unitary national jurisdiction without sub-state corporate tax divergence.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80/2002 on Anti-Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, as amended by Law No. 36/2017 and Law No. 154/2019; Executive Regulations issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 441/2002, as amended; Ministerial Decree No. 1919/2021 on Registration of Beneficial Owner Data in the Commercial Registry; Companies Law No. 159/1981; Investment Law No. 72/2017 and its Executive Regulations; Commercial Registry Law No. 34/1976; Unified Tax Procedure Law No. 206/2020; Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT Rulebook; directives of the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; preliminary regulatory review may accept a notarized bank letterhead version

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all founding shareholders, UBOs holding at least 25%, executive directors, and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List and sanctions-country programs, UK HMT Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Egyptian national lists maintained by the EMLCU and the Central Bank of Egypt. PEPs, including family members and close associates, are subject to enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, and source-of-wealth verification under Law No. 80/2002 and MENAFATF standards. All screening results must be documented, retained for at least five years, and refreshed at least annually during KYC renewal.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) One-Stop-Shop electronic platform (https://www.gafi.gov.eg) together with the Commercial Registry automated network (CRNet) operated by the Ministry of Trade and Industry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be in Arabic. A foreign-language transliteration may be registered only as a secondary name representing the exact phonetic counterpart of the Arabic name. The name must not be identical or deceptively similar to any existing reserved or registered name, and it must reflect the commercial or industrial activity, such as manufacturing of pumps, cryogenic equipment, or LNG equipment. Names implying public or governmental character, foreign state sponsorship, or activities outside the licensed scope are rejected.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Insurance, Reinsurance (require prior Central Bank of Egypt or Financial Regulatory Authority licensing)
Free Zone (requires licensed free-zone establishment status)
Holding (subject to minimum capital and Financial Regulatory Authority thresholds)
Petroleum, Oil, Gas (triggers prior approval from the relevant energy regulator when forming the principal activity token)
Islamic, Sharia (requires prior clearance from the Ministry of Endowments)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Extension: a written extension request must be filed with the GAFI One-Stop-Shop before the reservation expiry; the name reservation may be renewed once for an additional 90 days. Rejection: within 15 working days of the official rejection notice, the applicant may file an administrative appeal to the GAFI Name Committee and the Ministerial Committee for Commercial Registries, citing the Commercial Registry Law and distinctiveness grounds; an alternative name containing an added distinctive descriptor may be resubmitted immediately without forfeiture of fees. If the administrative appeal is denied, judicial review may be initiated before the Administrative Court of the Egyptian State Council within 60 days of the final decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted as the sole solution for an industrial manufacturing LLC under ISIC 2813. The LLC must demonstrate physical commercial substance in Egypt through a notarized lease, preferably with a minimum three-year term, or through a title deed for the registered office; the manufacturing plant must be physically identifiable on site. A serviced office may be used only as a temporary correspondence address during the incorporation period.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: approximately 80% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 12 months after license issuance. GAFI, the Egyptian Tax Authority, and the Industrial Development Authority routinely verify physical premises, production equipment, headcount, payroll, and inventory. The enhanced AML risk tier of Medium_Risk_Enhanced elevates the likelihood of documented post-incorporation substance checks.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 159 of 1981 on Joint Stock Companies, Partnerships Limited by Shares and Limited Liability Companies, as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018 (LLC provisions, Articles 42-54); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 2310 of 2017).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - One-Stop Shop, Commercial Registry Division
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association (Incorporation Contract) of the Limited Liability Company
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for LLCs under Law 159/1981 as amended by Law 4/2018; however, the entire subscribed capital must be paid up in full at formation (cash or in-kind), evidenced by a bank deposit certificate or independent in-kind valuation; no escrow account is mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation of CryoPump Egypt LLC under Law 159/1981 is ratified; the share capital of EGP 1,000,000 divided into 10,000 ordinary shares is subscribed and allotted to the founding members; the registered office is adopted at Plot 12, Tenth of Ramadan Industrial Zone, Cairo; Eng. [A] is appointed General Manager and Mr. [B] Financial Manager, jointly authorized to operate bank accounts and execute contracts; [Auditor Firm] is appointed statutory auditor; management is authorized to file for the industrial license with the IDA, environmental review with the EEAA and civil defense certificate, and to take all ancillary actions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Department, Ministry of Justice (Real Estate Notarization Offices)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founding members must appear before the notary in person or through legally authorized attorneys-in-fact to authenticate the bilingual (Arabic/English) LLC incorporation contract and appoint the first managers. Non-resident founders must submit powers of attorney notarized in their home state and either apostilled under the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention where the issuing state is a party or consular-legalized by the Egyptian embassy. Pay the notarial tariff and obtain the notarized contract as the foundational instrument for all downstream registrations.
required_dossiers: GAFI name reservation certificate for the proposed LLC
Valid national ID or passport copies of all founding members
Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association (Arabic text controlling)
Legalized power of attorney for any absent founder
Bank capital deposit certificate evidencing full payment of subscribed cash capital or in-kind valuation report
Statement of lawful purpose under ISIC 2813 (cryogenic liquid pump manufacturing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the notary raises a drafting or legal-form defect, counsel files a corrective addendum deed rectifying the relevant clause and re-presents the same instrument; no loss of filing priority or substantive rights occurs.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI One-Stop Shop Registration and Commercial Registry Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - One-Stop Shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized incorporation contract and supporting dossiers to the GAFI One-Stop Shop. GAFI coordinates the Commercial Registry listing, issues the Commercial Register Extract, and assigns the entity identification number. Under the Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 deemed-approval rule, failure of GAFI to decide within the statutory window entitles the applicant to proceed. Concurrently open the corporate bank account and file the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) declaration under the AML Law when the bank performing KYC remits the account details.
required_dossiers: Notarized incorporation contract (original and two certified copies)
GAFI name reservation certificate
Commercial lease or usufruct agreement for the registered office address
Copies of founders' national IDs or passports
Bank capital deposit certificate
AML/CFT ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) declaration form
Completed GAFI LLC registration application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a query letter (e.g., on the object clause or capital proof), submit a written response with corrected documents within 10 working days; if GAFI remains silent after the statutory period, invoke the deemed-approval rule by filing a formal request for issuance of the Commercial Register Extract.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with the Egyptian Tax Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - GAFI integrated tax desk / governorate ETA office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the standard combined tax registration form to obtain the corporate Tax Card covering income tax, payroll withholding, and VAT under Law No. 67 of 2016. Register the commercial address now and the factory address upon issuance of the industrial license. If the company meets the e-invoicing threshold, activate the ETA e-invoicing portal account during the same registration cycle.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register Extract issued by GAFI
Notarized incorporation contract
Combined tax registration application form (Form 1 equivalent)
Lease contracts for the registered office and factory plot
Proof of tax file creation routed via the GAFI One-Stop Shop
Appointment deed of the authorized general manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Tax Card application is rejected for incomplete address data, resubmit with the notarized rental contract and, if necessary, obtain the senior officer's approval; ETA issues or corrects the Tax Card within 3 working days of complete documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Official Gazette (Al-Waqa'i' Al-Misriyya)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Official Gazette Office - via GAFI publication window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the statutory publication request attached to the incorporation contract and the Commercial Register Extract. The Official Gazette publishes the mandatory abstract of the LLC formation and its objects clause, providing third-party notice of the company's incorporation. Retain the stamped gazette extract as a supporting document for bank account opening and significant contracting transactions.
required_dossiers: Publication request form signed by the General Manager
Certified copy of the notarized incorporation contract
Commercial Register Extract
Proof of payment of the gazette publication fee
Tax Card copy for identification consistency
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Should the Gazette return the request for textual corrections, revise the abstract, reattach the registry extract, and resubmit; the publication date is reset to the corrected acceptance date without penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social Insurance and Labor Office Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance (NISA); Ministry of Manpower Labor Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the LLC as an employer with NISA within the statutory window to obtain the employer file number and assigned branch office; file employee declaration forms (Form 1 and Form 2) for all managers and initial staff. Notify the competent Labor Office of the industrial activity and the operating commencement date; post the labor policy and workplace safety notices at the principal location.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register Extract
Tax Card
Notarized incorporation contract
List of founders, managers, and initial employees with valid national IDs
Form 1 and Form 2 social insurance declarations
Factory lease or ownership certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: NISA may direct correction of salary declarations or wage records; submit amended payroll schedules preserving the original effective date and obtain the adjusted Form 2 confirmation within 5 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial License Application under Law No. 15 of 2017
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) - Industrial Licensing One-Stop Window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the industrial license application through the IDA licensing portal after satisfying pre-incorporation conditions. The facility is classified in Category B (medium-risk industrial activities) under the ministerial classification lists; the package includes the environmental review routed to the Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), the industrial safety file reviewed by the General Administration of Civil Defense, and the construction and operational layout approved by the IDA engineering committee. The IDA issues a construction license first and thereafter an operating license following completion inspection of the production line and safety systems.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register Extract and Tax Card
Certificate of ownership, usufruct, or long-term lease of the industrial land
Factory engineering layout and process flow diagrams
Preliminary environmental review with EEAA approval or no-objection letter
Industrial safety and fire protection design approved by the Civil Defense authority
List of machinery, manufacturing process description, and production capacity statement
Proof of financial solvency (bank statement or audited capital evidence)
Valid notarized power of attorney for the factory operator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If IDA issues a technical defect notice, remedy the comments within 30 days and resubmit; an unfavorable denial may be appealed to the Industrial Licensing Appeals Committee; failure of IDA to decide within the 60-day statutory window results in deemed approval under Law No. 15 of 2017.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) - Industrial Licensing One-Stop Window
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial Facility Operating License under Law No. 15 of 2017 (رخصة تشغيل منشأة صناعية)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B (Annex/List 2) - preliminary environmental review and screening report required; full baseline EIA is not mandated for cryogenic pump machining, assembly, pressure testing, and warehousing in the absence of heavy smelting, large coating lines, or hazardous chemical treatment; final tier assignment is confirmed during the IDA/EEAA pre-license screening.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Law No. 4 of 1994 as amended and Executive Regulations Decree No. 338 of 1995: industrial wastewater discharged to public sewer not to exceed pH 6.0-9.5, BOD5 600 mg/L, COD 700 mg/L, TSS 800 mg/L, oil and grease 100 mg/L; process VOCs from degreasing and painting booths captured at source with not less than 95% removal efficiency; hazardous wastes (spent coolants, paint sludges, solvents) stored, transported, and disposed of under EEAA waste-tracking manifests per Articles 33-35 of Law No. 4 of 1994.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: General Administration of Civil Defense (GACD), Ministry of Interior, fire safety inspection and pre-operational certification: approved fire pumps, hydrant networks, portable extinguishers, smoke and heat detection, emergency egress signage, plus cryogenic gas detection and forced ventilation in LNG pump test cells; GACD site inspection is gated to the final industrial operating license. Structural load certificate for the factory floor and test-stand foundations is issued by a licensed engineering office. Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) clearance under Labor Law No. 12 of 2003 and Ministerial Decree No. 211 of 2003 covering noise exposure, electrical grounding, compressed-gas cylinder safety, permit-to-work for hot works, personal protective equipment, medical surveillance, and annual evacuation drills; the Ministry of Manpower issues the workplace compliance certificate upon final inspection.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — unified tax administration via the official portal at www.eta.gov.eg and the 'inTax' / electronic invoice digital services platform (Egypt, Arab Republic; Member: Inclusive Framework on BEPS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing or operating through an Egyptian office, permanent establishment or branch in Egypt must: (1) appoint a tax representative with a duly notarized and legalized power of attorney; (2) secure a registered Egyptian address supported by a lease or title document; (3) complete incorporation or branch registration with the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) where a license is required (producing cryogenic pumps requires a statutory industrial license — Commercial Registry + Industrial Development Authority coordination); (4) file constitutional documents, board resolutions, passport copies and financial statements with the ETA under Law No. 91/2005 as amended by Law No. 30/2023 and recent 2025 amendments; (5) obtain the statutory Tax Card (TIN) and, where relevant, a separate VAT registration certificate issued by the ETA VAT department; (6) register in the ETA e-Invoicing/e-Receipts platform via web portal, API integration, or certified ERP solution; and (7) activate fiscal credentials for generating ETA-cleared invoices and QR stamping. Non-resident suppliers with a permanent establishment in Egypt are subject to the same TIN registration duty; entities acting solely at the free-zone/SCZone licensing regime follow special zone procedures, but zone entities still require a distinct tax identification code and must file periodic declarations to ETA even when using customs suspension.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — an Egyptian Limited Liability Company is a resident juridical person taxed on its worldwide income at the statutory corporate rate of 22.5% under Law 91/2005 (as amended, rate effective 2025; previously 20.5%). Non-resident entities are taxed exclusively on Egyptian-source income unless a Double Taxation Treaty provides otherwise. Industrial manufacturing profits derive from the head office/principal place of business allocation rules and the deeming provisions applicable to management and control; SCZone licensed companies within the Suez Canal Economic Zone may benefit from the special zone tax regime (Law No. 5/2022), including reduced or statutorily deferred profit taxation and streamlined customs/export treatment where a valid zone operating license is maintained.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Egyptian tax law applies a mandatory statutory entity-level classification; there is no elective check-the-box or pass-through mechanism. Partnerships (not applicable to the LLC structure) and joint ventures are fiscally opaque unless a specific decree provides otherwise. Egypt has enacted controlled-foreign-company and general anti-avoidance rules (including Article 33 bis of the Income Tax Law) that curtail hybrid mismatch outcomes and base-eroding structures; group/consolidated tax filing is not generally available, although amendments permit certain loss-offset or reorganization elections with ETA pre-approval (restructuring continuity-of-interest conditions).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual value of taxable supplies for compulsory VAT registration (Law No. 67 of 2016 and Executive Regulations), measured on a trailing twelve-month basis; producers of zero-rated goods may opt for voluntary registration regardless of turnover; suppliers of goods or services solely within designated exempt zones must verify whether the special-zone VAT suspension applies. Small suppliers with annual taxable turnover above EGP 250,000 may register under the simplified schedule at the ETA's discretion.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoice and e-receipt clearance under Law No. 67/2016, ETA Decision No. 208/2021, and subsequent amending decrees. Registered taxpayers must integrate with the central ETA clearance platform through the authorized API (or portal-based submission), transmit invoice data in the ETA JSON/XML schema before invoice issuance, and generate a machine-readable QR code and unique fiscal ID for every invoice. Clearance is real-time/automated; invoice validation includes TIN matching, commodity code cross-checks (ISIC/HS), and buyer/supplier rights verification, and any invoice rejected by the platform is treated as not issued for input-credit purposes, exposing the supplier to Article 20 late-payment and Article 69-70 civil penalties. The e-receipt mandate currently phases in by taxpayer turnover band; failure to integrate leads to suspension of electronic filing privileges and denial of input VAT offsets.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A manufacturer of cryogenic liquid pumps may apply VAT at 0% where: (1) tangible goods are sold to a non-resident buyer, ownership and risk pass to that buyer, and the goods physically depart the Egyptian customs territory within the statutory export window; (2) the export is evidenced by a validated Customs Export Declaration made through the NAFEZA single window; (3) an ETA-cleared electronic invoice carrying the statutory zero-rating reason code is issued in the exporter's name; and (4) the foreign currency consideration is collected through an authorized Egyptian bank in accordance with Central Bank of Egypt directives, including any CBE repatriation/offset rules. Services directly connected with exported goods (installation, off-shore technical commissioning, packing, international freight) may likewise qualify where rendered to a non-resident principal and substantiated by written contract plus bank documentation. Supplies into licensed SCZone beneficiaries enjoy a customs-duty suspension and, where statutorily applicable, zero-ratable treatment equivalent to export; the zone purchaser must hold a valid zone operator license and the goods must ultimately be exported or consumed in authorized zone operations.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration issued through the NAFEZA single window (Single Administrative Document) bearing the customs stamp and ED code
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill naming the Egyptian exporter as consignor/shipper
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit advice from an authorized Egyptian bank evidencing receipt of foreign currency funds
Commercial invoice accommodating HS/ISIC coding matching the ETA-cleared e-invoice serial number
Packing list, weight/certificate of origin, and any certificate required by the destination country (e.g., certificate of origin for GAFTA/COMESA preferential claims)
Copy of the export order/contract and Incoterms confirmation supporting transfer of risk to the non-resident buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA performs systemic cross-matching of zero-rated export e-invoices against NAFEZA customs exit data and CBE foreign-currency reports; discrepancies generate desk audits and automated assessment notices. Goods not physically exported, shipments returned, or invoices bearing false exit numbers result in mandatory 0% reversal and assessment of 14% standard-rate VAT, plus delay penalties computed from the original due date under Articles 19-20 of the VAT Law and late-filing penalties (starting at 1% per day payable from the due date of the return). Fraudulent export zero-rating declarations — including forged bills of lading, fictitious customs declarations, sham circular transactions, or documentation reflecting repatriation through non-authorized accounts — constitute tax evasion under Article 72 of Law 67/2016, punishable by imprisonment for a term of not less than one month and a fine of not less than EGP 20,000 and not exceeding EGP 100,000, with confiscation and clawback of any refunded VAT plus fines equal to two to five times the evaded tax; for repeat offences or organized evasion, imprisonment up to five years may be imposed together with director/manager disqualification and exclusion from the e-invoicing platform. The VAT statute of limitations for assessment and collection is six years, running from the date the return falls due, and the ETA has discretion to publish final evasion rulings and to suspend the taxpayer's electronic fiscal credentials during the investigation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) – Foreign Exchange Administration, acting under the Exchange Control Act No. 97 of 1947, the Central Banking and Monetary System Law No. 88 of 2003, and Law No. 194 of 2020 delegating FX supervision to CBE.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a liberalised current-account regime: imports and services payments, dividend remittances, and repatriation of profits are permitted through banks against ordinary supporting documentation and no separate CBE licence. Capital-account inflows such as equity injections, intra-group loans, and portfolio investments remain subject to CBE reporting/purpose codes, GAFI registration under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, and anti-money-laundering verification. Dividends/profit remittance do not require a pre-authorisation but can be delayed by temporary FX liquidity constraints; tax clearance from the Egyptian Tax Authority in the form of a certificate of no outstanding tax liability is normally required for sums exceeding the historical paid-in capital. Transfer pricing/audited accounts must support the distributable reserve calculation. The EGP is convertible at a market rate determined by banks; official CBE rate and interbank rate converge after the March 2024 unification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the current liberalised exchange regime, there is no mandatory conversion of full export proceeds into EGP and no fixed statutory surrender ratio. Exporters are required to repatriate export receipts into Egypt through a licensed local bank and file the receipt with CBE's electronic export proceeds form; the retained FX may be held in foreign-currency accounts, sold to the banking system at the interbank rate, or used for import/trade obligations. The practical statutory-completion timeline is within 90 days from the date of the customs export declaration or as extended by CBE circular in force at the time of remittance; entities in the SCZone benefiting from the 2023/2024 investment incentives should verify any applicable exporter registration and inward payment documentation rules.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (EGP and FX) and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account / Import LC and Export FX Collection Account
Operational Account and LC settlement account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low – as a standalone account provider for an Egyptian registered LLC. Offshore digital EMIs (Euronext / UK FCA e-money institutions, UAE payment firms) are not licensed to take deposits or execute EGP-denominated current-account transactions in Egypt and cannot satisfy CBE's 'beneficiary account in licensed Egyptian bank' requirement for import settlements. They may be used only as payment/correspondent rails within the European corridor after opening the primary treasury account at a CBE-licensed bank. Any EMI maintaining a segregated client account must document that it is not executing Egypt domestic clearing activity, otherwise it will trigger CBE unauthorised e-money business risk under Law 194/2020.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person appearance is the practical mandate. CBE Know-Your-Customer and Anti-Money-Laundering Unit (AMLU) directives require face-to-face identification of the entity's authorised signatories and the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) at the bank's Egyptian branch or a notarised/holographed power of attorney exercised by a locally resident agent for account-opening and signatory registration. Remote video onboarding is not a standalone substitute for the initial high-risk manufacturing-classified account; after the account is operational, video-based KYC refresh and e-signature are permitted for updates. Evidence of local presence such as the entity's Egyptian commercial registry extract, industrial/health-and-safety licence for the pump manufacturing plant, and physical premises inspection (often by the bank agent) is practically indispensable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity: non-resident shareholders, nominee layers, or a UBO not identifiable on commercial registry data
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Chart of ownership up to natural persons, passport copies of all ultimate owners with certified legalisation, UBO declaration on the bank's template, commercial register computer extract, memorandum and articles of association, board resolution appointing authorised signatories, GAFI certificate of incorporation, and power of attorney with foreign apostille/consular legalisation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of startup capital and high-value inward cash or crypto transactions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements for the previous 12 months at the direct parent/shareholder level, notarised board minutes approving capital injection, signed investment agreements, tax records for the origin of funds, evidence of sale/supply activity (LC contracts, purchase orders), and source-of-wealth statement supported by audited financial statements or tax returns, accompanied by a CBE terrorism-financing screening explanation letter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/screening findings for country/individual or red flags in export/import trade because of LNG/cryogenic end-user profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Industrial end-user statement / no-shipment-to-sanctioned-parties warranty, HMRC-style dual-use/ex-licensing analysis or Egyptian export-control approval as required by Ministry of Trade and Industry; full KYC pack for every counterparty; commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading; US/EU sanctions counsel memo; continuous name-screening evidence and bank declaration of absence of nexus to sanctioned vessels.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Banking tax non-compliance evidence: PE deemed in Egypt or unpaid withholding/export-import VAT
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tax card (tax identification) certificate, recent tax return filings and receipts, transfer pricing summary for intra-group sales, Egyptian VAT registration certificate and export exemption/zero-rating evidence, tax clearance certificate for profit remittance, and an explanatory memorandum reconciling revenue with tax filings.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity capital injection must be routed via SWIFT from the foreign parent's bank to the Egyptian operating LLC's account at a CBE-licensed bank using an MT103 with a clear beneficiary reference. The remittance purpose/description should use the CBE coding frame for 'direct investment – foreign company equity contribution', with the beneficiary name matching the commercial register and a unique CIB/Council-of-Ministers/GAFI investment file number if the facility is in the Suez Canal Economic Zone. The bank will require a copy of the GAFI import/export certificate or issuance from the General Authority for Investment, board resolution/proposed share capital increase minutes, a share subscription agreement, and an undertaking to file the CBE Form 441 (capital/debt operations) or the current equivalent e-reporting form; the receipt is then booked in the foreign-currency account and credit to the legal reserve is made according to the Egyptian accounting standards. No payment may be settled to a private offshore collection account before the Egyptian account is fully onboarded; the automated Clearing House ACH is only domestic EGP-denominated so cross-border funds must clear through SWIFT correspondent banking.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For import of pump components and foreign technical services, settlement rails are SWIFT MT103 payment orders, MT202 covers interbank reimbursement, and commercial letters of credit (confirmed, irrevocable at sight or deferred payment) issued through an Egyptian bank with cable/SWIFT MT700/MT707 amendment routing. The trade disbursement must be marked with the Egypt import purpose code and supported by customs declaration, air/sea waybill, verified supplier invoice, and any necessary original certificate of origin for tariff preference. SCZone-operating LLCs may settle imports for the assembly of cryogenic pumps from a foreign-currency sub-account; an EGP-denominated settlement is executed at interbank rate; a bank payment order to a supplier in EGP is not permitted in only foreign-currency trade, except for local supplier payments under commercial-grade evidence. For LNG/cryogenic equipment that is classified under dual-use export/import regimes, the compliance pack additionally includes the importing carrier's export permit or destination exemption certificate and inland customs approval. For foreign services (software licenses, engineering studies) the remittance route is MT103 with an 'international services invoice' audit and 10% WHT on non-resident service consideration where applicable, plus e-original of the contract to CBE bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (EGP/USD) with a licensed banking counterparty for up to the invoice/LC amount and a validated underlying trade transaction
Non-deliverable EGP/USD forward (NDF) executed offshore or via the bank's overseas branch, used only if permitted by CBE circular and subject to position/exposure limits
FX-USD/EGP foreign-currency-account sweep/swaps (deliverable swap) for scheduled export proceeds and import payments
Foreign-currency interest rate and currency swap (cross-currency swap) between USD fixed/floating and EGP where the hedge nomenclature reflects the loan or trade flows
Option-type embedded hedging in import/export forward trade contracts, if specifically backed by a CBE-approved treasury product letter and not prohibited as speculative derivative activity
Natural hedging through matched USD-denominated supplier payment and export-collections accounts, which suppresses the need for market instruments

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Form 19) with audited financial statements and applicable transfer pricing disclosure forms attached
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after fiscal year end (by April 30 for a calendar-year LLC, unless an alternative fiscal year has been pre-approved by the ETA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late-payment penalty of 2% of unpaid tax for each month or fraction thereof; late-filing administrative fines under Tax Procedures Law 73/2016 up to EGP 1,000,000 (approx. USD 20,000); tax clearance suspension blocking commercial registry renewal and industrial license renewal

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GAFI annual compliance filing of audited financial statements and general assembly resolutions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Companies Registration E-System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year end, simultaneous with or immediately after the annual general assembly (AGM); AGM must be held no later than June 30 for a calendar-year LLC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines under Companies Law 194/2020 and its executive regulations up to EGP 200,000 (approx. USD 4,000); suspension of GAFI registration file and blockage of subsequent notarial and banking transactions for continuing default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual commercial registry renewal (data refresh and recurring registration fee payment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Authority (administered through GAFI / Ministry of Trade electronic renewal platform)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On the annual anniversary date of the entity's commercial registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal surcharge applied per the Commercial Registry Law 34/1976; registry file flagged with active default status; prolonged non-renewal exposes the LLC to administrative strike-off followed by judicial dissolution proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership (UBO) register confirmation via the GAFI Beneficial Ownership E-Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI Beneficial Ownership Register (accessible to the Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit and AML authorities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the commercial registry renewal date; re-filed within 30 days of any quota (share) transfer or change in control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines under AML Law 80/2002 as amended by Law 154/2019 up to EGP 500,000 (approx. USD 10,000) and possible imprisonment of responsible officers for false, incomplete, or omitted UBO disclosures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual withholding tax reconciliation statement and payroll/corporate declarations reconciling monthly WHT returns (Forms 2 and 41)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - assigned Medium or Large Taxpayer Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months after the tax year end (by end of February for a calendar-year LLC), reconciling all monthly WHT and payroll stamp-duty returns
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly 2% delinquency penalty on under-declared or unreconciled amounts; employer personal liability for collected-but-unremitted withholding; fixed late-filing fines under Tax Procedures Law 73/2016

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for all Egyptian LLCs: Companies Law 194/2020 requires every LLC to appoint at least one certified auditor registered with the ETA, with no turnover or asset exemption; the ISIC 2813 industrial operation license (issued by the Industrial Development Authority) further imposes audited financial submissions, and the entity's Medium-Risk enhanced AML classification reinforces audit frequency requirements
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) issued by the Ministry of Investment and the Financial Regulatory Authority (EAS are substantially converged with IFRS); full IFRS is permitted or required for subsidiaries of listed groups and for entities issuing public securities

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Directors must continuously identify every natural person owning directly or indirectly more than 25% of the LLC's quotas or exercising ultimate control; the UBO declaration is confirmed annually on the commercial registry renewal date through the GAFI Beneficial Ownership E-Register and amended within 30 days of any quota transfer or control event; false or incomplete UBO data triggers criminal liability under AML Law 80/2002 as amended

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Headline rate is a flat 22.5% on taxable corporate profits. Eligible cryogenic pump manufacturers may benefit from Investment Law 72/2017 incentives, including up to 30–50% investment cost deductions for qualifying projects, accelerated depreciation on production machinery, and the Law 83/2002 Special Economic Zone regime (e.g. SCZone) that can provide income tax holidays of 5–10 years for licensed zone-based projects. Export-oriented free-zone companies may enjoy full exemption from corporate income tax on export revenue.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Egyptian corporate income tax return Form No. 19 for juridical persons, filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-filing portal at https://www.eta.gov.eg.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return with quarterly provisional tax payments (April, July, October, December).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing is due within four months after the fiscal year-end. For a calendar-year EG LLC, the return is due by 30 April.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Commercial Registration (CR) number, Tax ID Number (TIN), registered address, and fiscal year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the EG LLC’s full legal name and TIN as registered; identify the permanent establishment as the Egyptian entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business activity and industrial classification code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State exactly: 'Manufacture of liquefied natural gas (LNG) cryogenic pumps'; ISIC Rev.4 code 2813 and NAICS 2022 code 333911.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of transactions with related parties, parent company, foreign affiliates, and shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Aggregate all cross-border controlled transactions and attach the transfer pricing Local File if the EGP 10 million threshold is triggered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable income: revenue, cost of sales, deductible expenses, tax adjustments, loss carryforwards, credits, and the 22.5% tax due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Egypt-source attributable income of the EG LLC/PE is taxed; claim treaty credits or exemptions in the applicable DTA schedule.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing incurs a penalty of EGP 20,000–100,000; underpaid tax attracts a 2% monthly late-payment surcharge capped at 60% of the tax. Repeat violations may double administrative penalties and trigger criminal prosecution under Law 91/2005 as amended.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% gross withholding tax on cash and in-kind profit distributions paid by an EG LLC to non-resident shareholders, unless a specific DTA relief reduces the rate or the distribution is exempt under applicable investment-zone rules.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a DTA reduced rate: obtain a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the beneficiary’s tax authority; file the ETA DTA relief application with the Large Taxpayer Office before or at the time of distribution; attach ownership percentages, audited financial statements of the beneficiary, and a signed beneficial-ownership declaration proving the recipient is not a conduit. The reduced rate is applied at source only after ETA approval; a refund is available if tax was overwithheld.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: interest 20%, royalties 20%, and technical/international service fees 20%. Under most Egyptian double tax treaties, interest and royalty withholding can be reduced to 10–15%, and frequently to 10% for industrial royalties on manufacturing know-how, subject to beneficial ownership and limitation-on-benefits clauses.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 10,000,000 annual aggregate for related-party transactions requiring a Local File; the Master File is required where the Egyptian constituent group revenue exceeds EGP 1,000,000,000; country-by-country reporting notification follows group consolidated revenue of EGP 25,000,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt has not adopted GCC-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the ETA applies substance-over-form, beneficial-ownership tests, and general anti-abuse doctrines under Law 91/2005 and ministerial guidance. A cryogenic pump manufacturer must hold actual production premises, manufacturing equipment, qualified payroll, core operating decisions, and physical or digital inventory in Egypt. A shell invoice company with no operational substance will be re-characterized, and treaty benefits will be denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Suppressing LNG pump sale proceeds, overstating purchases or depreciation, issuing counterfeit supplier invoices, or booking fictitious operational costs to reduce Egyptian taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 91/2005 as amended: restitution of underpaid tax plus monthly late-payment surcharge (2% monthly up to 60% max), administrative fine of EGP 20,000 to EGP 100,000, and imprisonment up to five years for the responsible persons.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false returns may be personally liable for the full unpaid tax and penalties; veil piercing permitted; travel bans, asset freezes, and civil restitution orders are available.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Sham Factoring / Conduit Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the EG LLC as an empty conduit, routing actual cryogenic pump manufacturing through a related offshore entity, and using high-margin management or marketing invoices to strip Egyptian profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA re-characterizes the transactions under substance-over-form, disallows phantom deductions, applies the full 22.5% tax plus monthly surcharge, and may impose an additional penalty up to double the avoided tax; the Commercial Registry may deregister the shell.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors involved in the sham arrangement can be held jointly liable for the entire tax deficiency, debarred from board positions, and subjected to provisional seizure of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing / Thin Capitalization / Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing related-party royalties, intellectual property licenses, or intercompany debt at non-arm’s-length levels, or structuring the LLC with excessive intercompany debt and minimal equity to inflate deductible interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment increases taxable profit; penalty up to EGP 250,000 for documentation failure; the adjustment attracts 22.5% tax plus a 2% monthly surcharge; excess interest may be re-characterized as dividends and subject to 10% withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign incomplete or false transfer pricing disclosures face personal restitution; continued non-payment can lead to seizure of personal property and exclusion from the Egyptian banking system.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving proceeds from sanctioned counterparties, using layered payment vehicles through Letter of Credit or SWIFT wires to disguise illegal commissions, bribes, or black-market currency transactions in cryogenic pump contracts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Egyptian AML Law 80/2002: imprisonment from at least 3 years up to 15 years for aggravated laundering, fines of EGP 100,000 to EGP 10,000,000, confiscation of laundered funds, and freezing orders issued by the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors with signature authority over affected accounts may face criminal liability, travel bans, personal bank account freezes, and extradition in coordinated cross-border financial crime investigations.
